prize_parts.citation: for the theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 topological insulator phase, and the first experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall state in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: I keep B042 as my preferred single achievement after the full first-round exchange. The case rests on three things that I think survived scrutiny. First, the physics is a distinct discovery: Kane and Mele showed that time-reversal symmetry together with spin-orbit coupling allows a Z2 invariant for a band insulator, which gives helical edge states with no integer-quantum-Hall analogue (no external field, no quantized Hall conductance, protection by time-reversal rather than by a Chern number). This answers the chair's question about the 2016 prize. Thouless, Haldane and Kosterlitz were honoured for topological phase transitions and Chern-type invariants in the quantum Hall and Haldane-model setting, where time-reversal is broken; a time-reversal-invariant Z2 phase is a different symmetry class and was not anticipated by that work. Second, the prediction-then-measurement chain is short and checkable: Kane and Mele in 2005, Molenkamp's group observing the edge-channel conductance in HgTe quantum wells in 2007, then independent confirmation in InAs/GaSb and, for the three-dimensional case, in Bi-based materials. Third, this is the kind of result where first-principles band theory and measured spectra or transport meet, and where the interpretation has been stable for about fifteen years. On the credit, I propose that the citation name only what the three people did, the Z2 quantum spin Hall prediction and the first observation of the state, and say nothing about the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang HgTe proposal, the three-dimensional materials or the quantum anomalous Hall effect. That wording is accurate, it does not claim the whole field, and it leaves Xue's experiment to be judged on its own. I am deliberately not stacking B012: Mehlig and Olsson convinced me that the quantum anomalous Hall effect depends on magnetic doping and is a separate result, and Olsson showed that B042 is the version that credits Mele.
statement.case_against: The credit remains the weak point and I do not think any wording removes it. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang identified HgTe as the platform that told Molenkamp where to look, and Zhang's death means the committee cannot recognise that step; Fu, Kane, Mele, Moore, Balents, Roy and Hasan carried the idea to three dimensions, and these people are outside any three-name cap. Kroll has said that he would need a convincing answer on this before ranking B042 above B037, and I cannot give him a complete answer, only the narrower one that the named trio is the traceable original chain for the two-dimensional quantum spin Hall effect. Second, the 2016 prize leaves some colleagues feeling that topology has been honoured, and Johansson and Mehlig report that this feeling exists; my argument about symmetry classes is a physics argument, not a guarantee of how it will be received. Third, B037 has the broadest support in the room (four preferred, two first places in the openings, no scientific objection recorded) and a two-name credit that is simpler than mine. If the priority history of the magic-wavelength proposal is confirmed from primary papers, I believe B037 is at least as defensible as B042 on credit and maturity, and I would not want to block it.

responses.point: Kroll prefers B037 as an unambiguous instrument-level invention with independent reproduction at the 1e-18 level and a two-name credit, and says he would need a convincing answer on the BHZ omission before ranking B042 above it.
responses.response: I accept that the lattice clock is the cleaner credit, and that independent agreement between clocks in Tokyo, Boulder, Paris and Braunschweig is the kind of reproducibility I weigh most. On BHZ I can only give you the narrow answer: the claim in B042 is the Z2 invariant and the first observation of the quantum spin Hall state, and Molenkamp's measurement tested the Kane-Mele prediction independently of why HgTe was chosen. I do not think this fully answers you. Where I differ is that I do not accept 'no new physics has yet been seen' as an argument against B042 in the way it counts against a clock, because B042 is itself a discovery of a new quantum state of matter. That is the trade I see: B037 has the better credit, B042 the stronger discovery.

responses.point: Lindroth ranks B037 first, values the match between a clean conceptual idea and precision measurement, and admits she recalls the priority history of the magic-wavelength proposal from memory and that familiarity may inflate her judgement.
responses.response: I appreciate that you flag your own memory and familiarity, because it is the honest way to handle it and it is why I cannot use your account as the evidence. Katori's proposal and first strontium demonstration, and Ye's route to 1e-18, may be exactly as you describe, but a final vote should not rest on recollection. I would like to see the two or three primary papers named in a short note, with dates, before the ballot. My reading of the physics is that the magic-wavelength lattice is a distinct step from ion clocks: the many-atom interrogation is a different regime from a single trapped ion. If that note supports the two-name split, B037 is my first alternative and I would move to it.

responses.point: Olsson moved from B012 to B042 because it credits Mele, regrets losing Xue's quantum anomalous Hall experiment as a separate discovery, and would keep the citation tied to the quantum spin Hall observation rather than to ARPES.
responses.response: I agree with you on the citation and have changed my wording accordingly: it now says 'first experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall state in HgTe quantum wells' and does not mention ARPES. In round 1 I cited ARPES as support for the case and I accept your distinction that it confirms the 3D phase but is not the original experiment. I also agree with you that the quantum anomalous Hall effect is a separate discovery. I would not add it as a second part, because the committee has agreed that B012 and B042 are one field and stacking them would also bring Xue in as a fourth name, outside the three-person limit.

responses.point: Mehlig prefers the narrower B042 framing over B012, accepts that credit is the weak point, and says that if the committee cannot accept the omissions, B037 is the better choice and he would not stand in the way.
responses.response: I think we are in nearly the same place. The chair asked what distinguishes Z2 insulators from the Thouless-Haldane-Kosterlitz lineage, and I would give the answer you gave in round 1: time-reversal symmetry plus spin-orbit coupling, a Z2 and not a Chern invariant, helical edge states and no net Hall response. I would add one test for the other members, namely that a prize on Chern insulators and the quantum Hall setting cannot be read to cover this phase, and the 2016 citation does not mention it. Like you, I would accept B037 as a fallback, but unlike you I am not yet willing to say that the BHZ omission makes B042 the weaker option, because the Kane-Mele and HgTe link is traceable without it.

responses.point: Pearce, as chair, builds on B037 for its calibration, systematics and independent confirmation, takes B042 as his first alternative, and says he would defer to Mehlig and me on whether the three names give a fair reading.
responses.response: Thank you for the deference, and I will try to deserve it. On fairness, the three names correspond to the original proposal of the Z2 state, its coupling to a realistic material class through Kane and Mele's own spin-orbit estimate, and the first observed signature. They do not correspond to the whole field and the citation should not suggest that. I agree with your own criterion, calibration and independent confirmation, and by that criterion B042 is well placed too: the HgTe conductance was reproduced by other groups and the Z2 state seen in other material systems. I do not see a strong reason for the chair to prefer one of the two on maturity, so the choice depends on credit and on the overlap questions, which we have still not closed for either.

responses.point: Danielsson prefers B006 as the experimental discovery never recognised, but says the three-name leadership credit is a compromise and that B037 is better if the committee cannot defend it.
responses.response: I remain outside the physics of B006 and cannot judge who was decisive, but I share the committee's worry that Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee are leadership names, and you have said yourself that you would fall back to B037. I am glad that you will not insist. I would add that if B042 loses out to B037 I would not feel the committee had made a poor decision, and that your remark on the order of preference, B037 before B042 if B006 fails, is a reasonable one.

uncertainties: Whether the priority history of Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and first strontium lattice clock, relative to Ye, the Paris group and the Boulder and NIST work, is as clean as the two-name credit assumes; I cannot check this and the AMO members have so far relied on memory.

Whether a citation for Kane, Mele and Molenkamp can be worded narrowly enough that it honours the Z2 prediction and the HgTe observation without being read as dismissing Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and the 3D work, and whether Kroll would accept it.
Whether other members find the symmetry-class argument against overlap with the 2016 prize persuasive, or still regard topology as honoured.
Whether B018 will look mature enough in a few years, once the correlated phases and superconducting mechanism are better understood; I no longer hold it as a first choice.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. I have no known personal, supervisory or institutional connection to Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, Katori, Ye, MacDonald, Bistritzer or Jarillo-Herrero. My field of first-principles electronic structure and magnetism is close in subject to B042 and B018, as the chair noted, and that is a matter of expertise and a possible familiarity bias, not a personal tie. I am outside atomic, molecular and optical physics and particle physics, and I have tried to defer on B037 and B006 where my knowledge is limited.
